result.recommendation: Retain generic music groundwork and the historical evidence below. Do not create, commission, bundle or import an actual musical Rosary. The researched recordings and scores are not selected for app content.
result.researchLimit: This is a bounded search, not evidence that no other openly licensed recording exists. No audio was downloaded or listened to, so performance pronunciation, all sung clauses, editing boundaries, audio quality and actual session lengths remain unverified.

appContract.format: An optional audio.json declares .opus files under audio/ inside a .prosaryprayer bundle. Audio is Ogg Opus, not an Ogg Vorbis file renamed to .opus.
appContract.musicRole: role: music; use the actual sung language from the manifest and the session's applicable variantId. Chapters begin at zero with increasing start times and omit stepIndex. Music does not seek or advance prayer steps; timer advancement remains available.
appContract.selection: A matching narration wins over music, then the first matching music declaration wins. There is no independent music track selector or narration/music mixer.
appContract.flowBoundary: Current recording controls and matching are in generic CustomDevotionFlow, not the built-in type: rosary flow. The user has excluded an actual musical Rosary, including any corresponding recording/player integration in the built-in Rosary flow.
appContract.authoringBoundary: Compose's wizard is narration-only and rejects music metadata it cannot preserve. Music bundles currently need manual authoring followed by the ordinary validator and pack tools.
appContract.languageBoundary: Translated subtitles, a translated catalogue page, or prayer text overlays do not make an Italian or Latin recording Hebrew, Arabic, French or another spoken language. Instrumental background independent of prayer language is future work.
appContract.credits: Keep creator, performer, recording owner, source URL, license/version and any editing/transcoding notes with the bundle. Third-party audio retains its source license; it does not inherit the first-party BSD-2-Clause or CC0 dedication.

compositionAndRecordingAreSeparate.finding: The U.S. Copyright Office distinguishes the underlying composition, including accompanying words, from a particular recording. A recording's authors can include performers and its producer; owning or clearing one work does not substitute for clearing the other.

layersToIdentify: Prayer wording and any modern translation or meditation
Any accompanying artwork or subtitle translation

licenseSources.finding: CC BY-SA 3.0 permits redistribution and adaptation, including commercially, with attribution and its applicable ShareAlike conditions. It prohibits additional legal or effective technological restrictions. Distribution must retain the audio's license rather than present it as first-party BSD or CC0.

CC0 waives the affirmer's copyright and related rights to the extent allowed by law. Other people's rights and rights in separately produced performances or recordings are not established by a score's CC0 status.

rightsEvidence.historicalPermissionConsiderations: App or prayer-pack redistribution of protected music would require the actual composition/arrangement and recording owners to cover offline storage, format conversion, chapter metadata, edits, repository distribution where relevant, stores and performers/co-owners. This is historical research, not a planned permission request. No contact has been made.
rightsEvidence.licenseDistributionConstraints: CC BY-SA audio retains its downstream access, notices, ShareAlike conditions and prohibition on additional restrictions. These findings do not select the researched audio for app or prayer-pack inclusion.

recordingCandidates.title: Schola Gregoriana — Ave Maria
recordingCandidates.kind: Individual sung prayer; not a complete Rosary
recordingCandidates.languageEvidence: The Catholic Bishops' Conference of England and Wales explicitly identifies its reuse as Latin sung Hail Mary. The Commons source describes Gregorian Vespers in honour of St Vincent Pallotti and links the corresponding chant score; this is not Schubert's song.

provenance.performer: Schola Gregoriana of the Pallottine Seminary in Ołtarzew, Poland
provenance.rightsHolderPermissionEvidence: The file description publishes a rights-holder email allowing the named Vespers recordings under free licenses; Wikimedia marks permission confirmed.

recordingCandidates.matchingScoreLead: GregoBase 1860, Ave Maria (Salutatio Angelica), Liber Usualis 1961 p.1861 / Chants of the Church 1956 p.86; its browsed GABC contains the complete Latin prayer including the second petition and Amen. The Commons recording's linked score is a separate CC BY-SA 4.0 image asset, not covered by the recording's 3.0 notice.
recordingCandidates.decision: Historical research only: reuse license has strong asset-specific provenance, while listening and exact prayer-text review remain unperformed. No recording is selected for inclusion, and the user excludes an actual musical Rosary.

recordingCandidates.title: Mary, Queen of Peace Meditation Guide & Sung Rosary

recordingCandidates.licenseFinding: Purchase and personal free-download/streaming links do not publish a redistribution license for embedding the master or arrangement in Prosary.
recordingCandidates.decision: Historical research only: the described full sung recording is permission-dependent and was not listened to or cleared. No permission request, authoring or app inclusion is planned.

recordingCandidates.accessFinding: Official pages were available in search extracts; a later direct English page fetch returned a cache-miss error. No recording or downloadable master was inspected.
recordingCandidates.licenseFinding: No explicit app/master redistribution license established by the inspected pages. A mission to offer performances or make prayer freely accessible is not itself a recording license.
recordingCandidates.decision: Historical research only: no redistribution license or multilingual sung-audio coverage was established. No permission request or app inclusion is planned; translated site pages and subtitles do not establish audio-language editions.

scoreCandidates.title: Ave Maria (Salutatio Angelica)
scoreCandidates.transcriber: Andrew Hinkley, with later corrections recorded by GregoBase
editionSources: Chants of the Church, Solesmes 1956, p.86
scoreCandidates.textFinding: The actual GABC was read. It sets the complete standard Latin Hail Mary, through the second petition and Amen, rather than the shorter offertory text or Schubert's original German poem.
scoreCandidates.decision: Historical research only: the transcription has an explicit CC0 dedication and contains the complete prayer. Its status does not license third-party recordings. No score or new musical Rosary recording is selected for inclusion.
